parsed.why: Protective state with enacted anti-discrimination law, facilities access, hate-crime coverage, and a documented high-court ruling for trans care. Pulled down by the 2026 facility-trespass arrest, a state-level document ban in the parent regime, and national funding pressure. Ballot counter-pressure is unresolved. Sits Elevated, near the parent line, with some protective upward movement.

Low-risk tier with explicit gender-identity discrimination ban enforced by a human relations commission, X markers on licences, and no-surgery marker changes via physician note. No facility-exclusion or trespass statute. Lacks a statutory hate-crime provision and a bill is pending, so it does not reach the top tier.

Documented universal exposure: a state facility statute with criminal trespass, a 2024 licence-marker refusal treated as fraud, and a birth-certificate freeze. Also adult gender-affirming care restrictions and a documented arrest. Only partial protection in some counties. Lands in Do Not Travel territory.

Surgical requirement for birth-certificate changes with no workaround, bars on minor and prisoner care, and a stated reversal on licence marker policy. Hate-crime law covers gender identity but no non-discrimination statute. Thin direct traveller exposure but strong documented state restriction keeps it in High Risk.

Explicit public-accommodation protection for gender identity with civil-rights enforcement, X markers and surgery-free marker changes, marriage recognition, and bias-crime enhancements. A bias-protection bill and advocacy tier ranking corroborate. Only minor weak spots (no recent facility rule, parental-notification fight unresolved).
